from typing import Any

from lfx.base.io.text import TextComponent
from lfx.io import BoolInput, MultilineInput, Output
from lfx.schema.message import Message


class TextInputComponent(TextComponent):
    display_name = "Text Input"
    description = "Get user text inputs."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/text-input-and-output"
    icon = "type"
    name = "TextInput"
    legacy = True
    replacement = ["input_output.ChatInput"]

    inputs = [
        MultilineInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Text",
            info="Text to be passed as input.",
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="use_global_variable",
            display_name="Use Global Variable",
            info="Enable to select from global variables (shows globe icon). Disables multiline editing.",
            value=False,
            advanced=True,
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Output Text", name="text", method="text_response"),
    ]

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dict, field_value: Any, field_name: str | None = None) -> dict:
        if field_name == "use_global_variable":
            if field_value:
                # Enable global variable mode: single-line with password masking and globe dropdown
                build_config["input_value"]["multiline"] = False
                build_config["input_value"]["password"] = True
            else:
                # Default mode: multiline text editing
                build_config["input_value"]["multiline"] = True
                build_config["input_value"]["password"] = False
        return build_config

    def text_response(self) -> Message:
        return Message(
            text=self.input_value,
        )

code.value:
"""Render a file built up in Langflow's sandboxed filesystem as a rich, real, multi-file
artifact in Fenrix Chat, without any LLM ever reading the file's full content back.

Pairs with Langflow's own `FileSystemTool` component: an agent appends chunks to a
file across as many tool calls as it needs (via `append_file` - each call only
carries the new chunk, never the accumulated total, so building a large document
costs no more tokens than the chunks themselves). This component is the flow's
final output - it does NOT read the file's content at all; it emits a real,
browser-loadable URL (`mimeType: "text/uri-list"`, a first-class @mcp-ui/client
resource type rendered as `<iframe src="...">`) pointing at
`agentic/api/files_router.py`'s `/sandbox-files` route, so the browser makes real HTTP
requests for the file and any relative CSS/JS/images it references - a real multi-file
website works, not just one inlined HTML blob. Outputs the same
`Data(data={"mcp_ui_resource": {...}})` shape `FenrixArtifactComponent` does, so it
renders through the exact same already-verified bridge (`handle_call_tool` in
`api/v1/mcp_utils.py`) with no further changes there.

Both `path` and the sandbox sub-path are resolved automatically from the in-flight MCP
call's conversation/project scope (see `_resolve_sandbox_subpath()` on
`FileSystemToolComponent`) - the same scope the writer's own `FileSystemTool` node
resolves to, so the two are guaranteed to agree without the flow author keeping two
fields in sync by hand. The `root_path` input remains only as a manual fallback for
editor/test runs outside that MCP context.

Reuses FileSystemTool's own hardened path-resolution and read primitives rather than
reimplementing them - see `_resolve_effective_user_id`'s docstring below for why a
plain `self.user_id` isn't safe to use here.

Two ways to use this, depending on the flow:

- Same-flow, single call: wire the Agent's own output into `run_after` (its value
  is ignored) so this node has a real dependency edge and Langflow schedules it
  after the agent's writes. Found to be unreliable when the upstream is an
  Agent with bound tools - Langflow's own graph engine doesn't consistently mark
  such vertices `built` in time, so this node's read can silently return nothing
  even though the file was written correctly. Fine for a non-agentic upstream.
- Separate flows (recommended for anything agentic): one flow does the writing
  (Agent + FileSystemTool, no rendering step at all), a second, simple flow is
  just a Text Input feeding this component's `path` - wire that connection so a
  caller can pass the filename per call instead of hardcoding it. Two independent
  MCP tool calls instead of one, but avoids the same-run timing issue entirely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.inputs.inputs import HandleInput, MessageTextInput, StrInput
from lfx.io import Output
from lfx.schema.data import Data


class FenrixArtifactFileComponent(Component):
    display_name = "Fenrix Artifact File"
    description = (
        "Render a file from Langflow's sandboxed filesystem as a rich artifact in Fenrix Chat - "
        "place this as the flow's output, pointed at a file a FileSystemTool node built up."
    )
    icon = "Fenrix"
    name = "FenrixArtifactFile"

    inputs = [
        MessageTextInput(
            name="path",
            display_name="File Path",
            required=True,
            info="Path to the file, relative to the sandbox root - same convention as FileSystemTool. "
            "Can be typed literally or wired from an upstream Text Input so a caller can supply it per call.",
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="root_path",
            display_name="Sub-directory",
            required=False,
            advanced=True,
            info="Must match the FileSystemTool node's own Sub-directory value in this flow, if any set.",
        ),
        HandleInput(
            name="run_after",
            display_name="Run After",
            required=False,
            input_types=["Data", "Message", "DataFrame", "Table"],
            info="Connect the Agent's own output here purely to make this node run after it - "
            "the connected value itself is ignored. Without this, Langflow has no reason to run "
            "this node after the agent's file writes, since path/Sub-directory are plain typed "
            "values, not connections.",
        ),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Artifact", name="artifact", method="build_resource"),
    ]

    def _resolve_effective_user_id(self) -> str | None:
        """Mirror FileSystemTool's own `_resolve_user_id` priority (end_user_id first)
        so this always reads from the SAME per-user sandbox directory a FileSystemTool
        write in this same flow would have used.

        A plain `self.user_id` is NOT safe here: when a flow is served for a specific
        identified end user (the Fenrix Chat-via-MCP case this component exists for),
        `graph.end_user_id` - not the executing service account's own id - is what
        FileSystemTool's writes actually land under. Using `self.user_id` alone would
        silently resolve to the wrong directory rather than erroring.
        """
        graph = getattr(self, "graph", None)
        for candidate in (getattr(graph, "end_user_id", None), self.user_id):
            if candidate is None:
                continue
            cleaned = str(candidate).strip()
            if cleaned and cleaned.lower() not in {"none", "null"}:
                return cleaned
        return None

    def build_resource(self) -> Data:
        import os
        from urllib.parse import quote

        from langflow.agentic.api.files_router import encode_sandbox_subpath
        from lfx.components.files_and_knowledge.filesystem import (
            FileSystemToolComponent,
            get_current_sandbox_api_key,
        )

        fs = FileSystemToolComponent()
        fs._user_id = self._resolve_effective_user_id()  # noqa: SLF001 - bind to the same sandbox root the writer used
        fs._force_isolation = True  # noqa: SLF001 - always per-user, regardless of AUTO_LOGIN (matches agentic/api/files_router.py)
        # _resolve_sandbox_subpath() (not self.root_path directly) so this automatically
        # agrees with whatever conversation/project scope the writer used, without the flow
        # author needing to keep two fields in sync by hand - see its docstring. The
        # explicit `root_path` input remains the fallback for editor/test runs.
        fs.root_path = self.root_path or ""
        sandbox_subpath = fs._resolve_sandbox_subpath()  # noqa: SLF001

        try:
            resolved = fs._validate_path(self.path)  # noqa: SLF001 - reuse the exact hardened boundary/deny-list/symlink checks
        except PermissionError as exc:
            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc

        if not resolved.exists():
            msg = f"File not found: {self.path}"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if resolved.is_dir():
            msg = f"Path is a directory, not a file: {self.path}"
            raise ValueError(msg)

        # A real, browser-loadable URL (not inline HTML text) - lets the rendered iframe make
        # genuine HTTP requests for relative sub-resources (<link href="styles.css">,
        # <script src="app.js">), which an inline blob has nothing to resolve against.
        # mimeType "text/uri-list" is a first-class @mcp-ui/client resource type (confirmed
        # this session) rendered as <iframe src="..."> rather than srcDoc, with
        # allow-same-origin included in its default sandbox permissions - sufficient for a
        # real JS-driven multi-file site with no FenrixChat frontend changes needed.
        #
        # The api key and sandbox sub-path are path segments, not query params - confirmed
        # live that a query-param design breaks a plain relative reference like
        # `<link href="styles.css">`: a browser resolving that drops the current URL's
        # entire query string and just replaces the last path segment, so the resolved
        # request loses both the api key and the sandbox scope and 404s. See
        # files_router.py's get_sandbox_file docstring for the full explanation.
        public_base_url = (os.environ.get("LANGFLOW_PUBLIC_BASE_URL") or "").rstrip("/")
        # Read off the live graph object (set in simple_run_flow), not the
        # get_current_sandbox_api_key() ContextVar helper - confirmed live that the
        # ContextVar comes back empty here even though this same graph's
        # conversation_id/chat_project_id (also ContextVar-backed at the source) resolve
        # fine via _resolve_sandbox_subpath's graph-attribute read above. Falls back to the
        # ContextVar for callers with no live graph (e.g. a bare unit test).
        graph = getattr(self, "graph", None)
        api_key = getattr(graph, "mcp_api_key", None) if graph is not None else None
        if not api_key:
            api_key = get_current_sandbox_api_key()
        if not public_base_url or not api_key:
            msg = (
                "Cannot build a sandbox preview URL: "
                f"{'LANGFLOW_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is not set' if not public_base_url else 'no caller API key in scope'}."
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        url = (
            f"{public_base_url}/api/v1/agentic/sandbox-files"
            f"/{quote(api_key, safe='')}"
            f"/{encode_sandbox_subpath(sandbox_subpath)}"
            f"/{quote(self.path, safe='/')}"
        )
        result = Data(data={"mcp_ui_resource": {"mimeType": "text/uri-list", "text": url}})
        self.status = result
        return result
